reasons: Both answers are nearly equivalent: Structured Outputs with an enum, a separate reason field, a tagged ticket in the user message, a data-not-instructions rule, a code fallback, and a 30-50 ticket evaluation with parse-rate and accuracy metrics. A edges ahead with more few-shot examples (including a pure-injection case mapped to other), explicit try/except validation code, and a concrete test table covering tag-closing injection, English input and empty input. B's main code snippet indexes data['category'] directly without the fallback it recommends in prose, although it adds a useful json_object fallback path and a clearer statement that the enum guarantees format but not correctness.

A: Claims injection cannot produce arbitrary text or leaks, but the free-form 'reason' string field can still carry attacker-influenced text
